**Strategic Philosophy: “One Global Game Integrity Core, Certified Regional Monetization Integration Profiles”**

The failure mode in global live-service monetization is treating loot-box compliance, probability disclosure, pay-to-win (P2W) boundaries, and player-protection advocacy as “soft” localization tasks—solved by translating a single global Terms-of-Service, applying one loot-box probability table globally, and deploying identical “open-door” player-support tickets everywhere. If the publisher rolls out the same gacha interface to Belgium (where chance-based rewards are restricted or banned), Korea (where government-mandated disclosure formats and approval cycles are strict), Japan (where gift-giving events and cosmetic gacha are culturally embedded), the Gulf (where religious and cultural norms reshape both chance-mechanics and luxury-spending rituals), Brazil (where informal digital advocacy collectives organize rapidly around P2W accusations), and the US (where state-level litigation risk and cross-border advocacy coordination are accelerating), it will either **under-manage in high-formality, restriction-heavy markets** (triggering regulatory penalties, market bans, and government blacklists) or **over-manage in high-context, culture-driven markets** (destroying player trust, suppressing legitimate advocacy, provoking viral solidarity campaigns, and forcing underground player organization).

The correct model is a **modulated monetization platform**: a standardized global game-ethics core (probability-transparency baseline, anti-deceptive-pattern rules, age and spend-protection architecture, crisis-escalation protocol, algorithmic fairness in matchmaking/reward distribution, cross-region advocacy-monitoring registry) packaged into **region-specific “Monetization Integration Profiles”**—each with its own reward-mechanic boundary map (loot-box replacement vs. disclosure-enhanced gacha vs. deterministic direct-purchase), representation mechanism (player advisory board vs. government mediator vs. advocacy-group liaison), disclosure-documentation tradition, event-calendar logic, and local credibility mechanism. This allows the firm to defend regulatory compliance in the EU, satisfy government certification in East Asia, honor cultural gift-giving norms in Japan, navigate religious and luxury-spending ethics in the Gulf, stabilize adversarial advocacy dynamics in Brazil, and contain litigation risk in the US—without allowing one region’s monetization logic to contaminate another’s player experience.

---

### 1. The Four-Layer Monetization & Governance Architecture

| Layer | Scope | Function | Transparency / Governance Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1: Global Game Integrity & Monetization Ethics Core** | Global (all regional variants of the title) | Non-negotiable backbone: **no deceptive dark patterns** (hidden probabilities, false scarcity timers, manipulative bundle architecture); **probability disclosure** rendered in locally mandated formats where required; **age-gating and spend-protection** (hard caps for minors, crisis-spend alerts, parental controls); **algorithmic fairness audit** (matchmaking and reward-drop integrity); **data privacy** (player behavioral data governed by local privacy law but never sold/transferred across profiles without consent); **global crisis-escalation protocol** for advocacy, regulatory, or viral backlash; cross-region **“Monetization Integration Registry”** tracking every regional mechanic variant, disclosure filing, advocacy agreement, and regulatory sign-off. | Every region reports through the same monetization-integrity schema. No regional monetization director can waive L1 rules without Global Integrity Council sign-off. Registry is auditable by regulators and player representatives where locally required. Core gameplay, progression loops, and social systems remain globally unified—only monetization interface, reward mechanism, and disclosure packaging are modulated. |
| **L2: Regional Integration & Player-Protection Profile** | Region-specific clusters: **EU (BeNeLux)**; **Korea & China**; **Japan**; **Gulf**; **Brazil**; **US** | Defines the **mechanic-boundary matrix** (what is locally permitted: deterministic direct-purchase, battle-pass, cosmetic-only, gift-system, gacha with enhanced disclosure, or banned/replaced); **disclosure-form tradition** (government XML filing, in-app visual table, notarized legal document); **player-representation mechanism** (elected advisory board, certified advocacy liaison, government mediator, peer-verified community council); **event-calendar logic** (government reporting cycles, religious months, social gift-giving windows, advocacy-watch periods); and **local credibility mechanism** (player-trust portal, advocacy-group observation rights, government audit partnership). | Published in **“Regional Monetization Playbooks”**: “Profile A = EU Formal Restriction Protocol; Profile B = East Asian Disclosure & Certification Protocol; Profile C = Japan Cultural Consensus & Gift-Giving Protocol; Profile D = Gulf Religious & Luxury Mediation Protocol; Profile E = Brazil Emerging Advocacy & Collective Consensus Protocol; Profile F = US Litigation & State-Fragmentation Protocol.” No global live-ops director can impose Profile B disclosure rules onto Profile C gift-culture mechanics, or Profile A bans onto Profile E advocacy negotiations, without Regional Integration Council approval. |
| **L3: Validation & Certification Package** | Cluster-adapted rollout batches | Tiered reviews: **Foundation** (global core verification: no dark patterns, correct disclosure architecture, age/spend protection active); **Regional Certification** (local law alignment: Belgium/Netherlands ban-compliance, Korea/China filing approval, Japan cultural audit, Gulf religious-compliance review, Brazil advocacy-observation agreement, US state-risk mapping); **Pilot Launch / Soft Rollout** (limited-market feature release with local player advisory observation, advocacy-group monitoring window, government filing test, sentiment-benchmark setup); and **Conflict-Integration Drill** (simulated viral backlash, advocacy boycott, regulatory audit, cross-border solidarity campaign—testing escalation speed, translation accuracy, and local credibility-pathway integrity). | Validation budget allocated by **regulatory-exposure tier** (market-access risk, advocacy-coordination velocity, penalty magnitude, government-approval dependency), not by revenue share or player-count alone. Pilot rollout rounds are mandatory before full-scale monetization feature release in every region. |
| **L4: Trust & Governance Profile** | Local / Cluster | **Local Monetization Integrity Director** (not remote HQ live-ops manager); **player-representation structure** (advisory board of verified community leaders, formal advocacy-group liaison, government mediator, or hybrid); **local legal/compliance partner**; **localized transparency portal** (probability tables, spend-protection dashboard, reward-mechanic explanation in local language with visual—not only legal-text—formatting); **real-time advocacy/viral-monitoring command** (local-language sentiment analysis, cross-border solidarity-tracking); and **crisis-escalation pathway** (regulatory, judicial, mediated, or community-correction route). | Every mechanic change, disclosure filing revision, spend-protection update, event-calendar shift, advocacy agreement, and sentiment spike is traceable back to L3 evidence and L2 labeling. Playbooks are standardized globally but executed by locally embedded monetization-governance teams—not centralized global product managers. |

### 2. Regional Monetization Integration Profiles: The Six Divergent Regimes

The past failure—“one global monetization template”—manifests when a Belgium-compliant deterministic purchase model is forced onto Japan’s gift-event culture, when Korea-style government XML disclosure is pasted onto Gulf luxury-event framing without religious-context adaptation, or when US-style litigation defense language is deployed in Brazilian informal advocacy forums, destroying trust.

| Dimension | **EU (Belgium / Netherlands)** — Formal Restriction Benchmark | **Korea & China** — Mandatory Disclosure & Government Certification | **Japan** — Cultural Consensus & Gift-Giving Scale Anchor | **Gulf (GCC)** — Religious & Luxury Mediation Protocol | **Brazil** — Emerging Advocacy & Collective Consensus | **US** — Litigation & State-Fragmentation / Advocacy Coordination |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Strategic Role** | Sets the global standard for **mechanic prohibition/replacement** (no loot-box chance-rewards) and **strict documentation**; highest regulatory-penalty exposure; GDPR-linked behavioral-data rules make transparency structural. | Sets the global standard for **formal government-facing disclosure** and **approval-cycle discipline**; probability formats are legally prescribed; government blacklisting is a real market-access risk. | Largest mature gacha/spend-market; **gift-giving (omiyage-style) events**, cosmetic prestige, and limited-time social rituals dominate revenue; player trust depends on **perceived fairness and social harmony**, not just legal compliance. | High-value spending per user; **religious norms on chance (maysir/gambling)** and gender/mixing representation reshape both mechanic and event design; luxury and exclusivity are culturally legible, not predatory. | Fastest-growing advocacy-coordination risk in Latin America; **informal digital collectives** organize via WhatsApp/TikTok around P2W accusations; price sensitivity is high; government self-regulation is emerging but weak. | No federal loot-box ban yet, but **state-level bills** (WA, CA, NY risk corridors) and **cross-border advocacy coordination** (consumer groups linking EU bans to US demands) accelerate; litigation discovery risk is high. |
| **Regulatory / Cultural Context** | Loot boxes with **real-money chance rewards are banned/restricted**; deterministic direct-purchase, battle-pass, or cosmetic-only models required; strict advertising and age-protection enforcement; national gaming authorities active. | **Mandatory probability disclosure** in legally specified formats; filing with government agencies (GRAC/Korean authorities; Chinese National Press and Publication Administration / Ministry of Culture); approval required for updates affecting monetization; P2W mechanics heavily scrutinized. | No mandatory probability law comparable to Korea, but **Consumer Affairs Agency** monitors deceptive practices; gacha is culturally normalized but **“complete gacha” (kompu gacha)** is banned; gift-currency and event-social norms require **face-saving correction pathways** if community rejects a feature. | **Islamic finance and ethics norms** restrict explicit gambling/chance; government content-review boards (Saudi GCAM, UAE NMC) evaluate games; luxury-item exclusivity is acceptable if framed as **status/charity/gifting**, not chance-dependency; gender/modesty rules affect cosmetic events. | **Consumer-protection advocacy (Procon, Idec)** growing; **informal player unions/collectives** digital-first; no strict federal loot-box law yet but bills proposed; **pricing/power balance** (P2W) is the primary advocacy trigger, not disclosure format alone. | **State legislatures** considering disclosure or restriction bills; **FTC and state AGs** investigating dark patterns; **class-action risk** over undisclosed probabilities or deceptive bundles; **advocacy groups** (Consumer Federation, international partners) coordinate campaigns linking Belgium bans to US demands. |
| **Player Organization / Advocacy Reality** | Formal, hierarchical advocacy and regulatory bodies; **indirect, documented engagement** required; criticism routed through official complaints and media regulators; management must document compliance, not merely “consult.” | Formal, state-facing: government filing and audit are primary actors; player advocacy exists but **government certification dominates** market access; direct public confrontation is less effective than regulatory non-compliance. | **High-context, collective, digital-first**; informal community leaders (streamers, guild heads, event organizers) have peer legitimacy without election; **consensus through harmony and face-saving**; viral Twitter/X and 5ch backlash is rapid; government mediators preferred over litigation. | **Government mediator + community elder/religious advisory** dynamics; public shaming violates norms; private revision with authority approval restores trust; luxury-community influencers operate by invitation/status, not election; advocacy is less adversarial than in Brazil/US. | **Rapid digital escalation** via messaging apps and social video; informal leaders emerge without formal mandate; direct confrontation and boycott calls probable; legal representation emerging but not universal; government prefers mediated, code-based resolution if available. | **Formal advocacy organizations** (Consumer Federation, state-based groups), **litigators**, and **media-coordinated campaigns**; players organize through Reddit, Discord, and formal petitions; cross-border solidarity is structured and legally sophisticated. |
| **Monetization / Engagement Risk (Past Failure Mode)** | Applying a global “gacha with disclosure” template; failing to replace chance mechanics with deterministic alternatives; treating compliance as “marketing copy update”; ignoring GDPR-linked player-behavior transparency obligations. | Applying EU-style “alternative progression” without Korean government filing format; failing to submit updated probability XML before rollout; treating disclosure as cosmetic rather than legally binding; missing approval-cycle timelines. | Forcing EU-style deterministic purchase onto gift-event culture; applying Korea-style legalistic disclosure tables without visual/social context; ignoring face-saving dynamics—public feature rejection without private revision destroys long-term community cooperation. | Applying Western “loot-box disclosure” framing that highlights chance/dependency (religiously sensitive); ignoring gender/content norms in luxury cosmetic events; failing to provide government-mediator pathway for community concern; violating exclusivity/status framing that justifies high-value spend. | Suppressing collective organization through “independent player” rhetoric; applying Japan-style private-revision norms without accommodating adversarial advocacy dynamics; failing to document every interaction (creating liability); ignoring price-access and P2W balance as advocacy triggers. | Applying Brazil-style informal negotiation norms to formal litigation risk; failing to document every disclosure change for discovery; ignoring state-level legislative variation; treating advocacy as “PR crisis” rather than structural legal and market-access risk. |
| **Specification Translation Risk** | “Loot box” definitions vary by jurisdiction; replacement mechanics (direct purchase, deterministic reward paths, cosmetic-only) must be engineered locally and documented for regulators; price-display and age-gating must match national advertising codes precisely. | Disclosure formats are **legally prescribed** (probability tables, item lists, approval stamps); translations must match government-approved terminology; updates to reward mechanics trigger **re-filing obligations**; “event calendar” is tied to government reporting windows. | Gift-event framing requires **local-language social context** (seasonal gifting, social reciprocity, prestige signaling); cosmetic items carry different status meanings; “agreement” is verbal/community-verified first, formalized in app-update notes later; transparency reports must be **visual and social**, not legal-text-heavy. | Luxury-item descriptions must avoid explicit “chance/gambling” framing; price points must align with **local luxury norms** (high-value acceptable if exclusive and status-conferring); gender/modesty filters applied to cosmetic events; disclosure, where present, framed as **transparency/ethics** rather than “gambling warning.” | Multilingual engagement (Portuguese + English master for advocacy documentation); “agreement” with advocacy groups often requires **public statement and private revision pathway**; P2W mechanics must be **clearly separated** from progression/competition systems in local terms; pricing must reference local income benchmarks, not global USD parity. | State-level disclosure requirements may diverge; litigation-hold documentation requires **English-language master archive with state-specific annotations**; advocacy demands often mix federal, state, and cross-border (EU-linked) claims—specs must separate negotiable (feature change) from non-negotiable (global anti-dark-pattern rules). |
| **Content / Policy Framing** | **Deterministic progression**, direct cosmetic/store purchase, battle-pass; calendar tied to regulatory audit and national advertising-enforcement windows; no seasonal “loot-box events.” | **Certified gacha/probability table**, government-filed updates; calendar tied to approval filing deadlines and government audit cycles; event mechanics must be filed before activation. | **Gift-giving events, cosmetic prestige seasons, social-harmony bundles**; calendar tied to cultural gift windows (New Year, Golden Week, Obon-style reciprocity); probability disclosure present but framed as **trust/fairness**, not government warning. | **Exclusive luxury drops, charity-linked prestige events, status-cosmetic seasons**; calendar tied to religious months (Ramadan, Eid) and government content-review windows; mechanics emphasize **exclusivity and choice**, not chance-dependency. | **Direct-purchase competitive balance, affordable bundle tiers, community-observed fairness updates**; calendar tied to advocacy-watch periods and government self-regulatory reporting; P2W separation is the central policy message. | **State-compliant disclosure layers**, deterministic alternatives in high-risk states, litigation-defensible documentation archive; calendar tied to legislative session windows and advocacy-campaign cycles; cross-border messaging must be coordinated but locally executed. |
| **L2 Engagement / Governance Protocol** | • **Formal, hierarchical, documented**: all mechanic changes filed and documented; player/advocacy interaction routed through official complaint and regulatory channels; private clarification with authorities before public feature change; crisis response co-reviewed with local gaming authority. | • **Government-facing formal documentation**: every update submitted in prescribed format; government mediator/approval body consulted; player advocacy engaged through formal observation rights (not adversarial strike); bilingual filing (local + English master). | • **Community-consensus checks**: peer-verified community leaders (streamers, guild heads) engaged before feature rollout; government Consumer Affairs consulted; direct digital-monitoring with sentiment analysis in Japanese/English; **face-saving correction pathway**: private revision with leader consultation before public launch. | • **Government mediator + luxury-community advisory**: private engagement with GCAM/NMC reviewers and community influencers; face-saving revision pathway; digital command monitors sentiment in Arabic/English; crisis response within hours to prevent viral escalation; **status/exclusivity framing** verified with local cultural advisors. | • **Advocacy-collective bridge**: peer-verified informal leaders and formal advocacy-group liaison; direct negotiation boundary clear: global anti-dark-pattern rules are non-negotiable; P2W separation, price fairness, and feature transparency are locally bargained/revised; government mediator engaged in formal rounds; bilingual documentation mandatory. | • **Formal advocacy & litigation liaison**: certified consumer-law and state-compliance partner; advocacy-group observation rights; direct formal documentation for every disclosure change; state-level legislative tracking integrated; crisis response is judicial/political, not merely “communications”; cross-border advocacy coordination monitored and contained through separate state pathways. |

### 3. Monetization Boundaries: The Modulated Matrix

A single global loot-box probability table and event-calendar cannot govern EU prohibition, East Asian government filing, Japanese gift-culture, Gulf religious framing, Brazilian advocacy dynamics, and US litigation risk simultaneously.

| Boundary Category | **Global Non-Negotiable (L1)** — Applies in All Profiles | **Regionally Modulated (L2)** — Determined by Local Profile | **Explicitly Excluded / Contained** — To Prevent Cross-Contamination |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Reward Mechanic & Chance Structure** | **No deceptive dark patterns** (hidden drop logic, false scarcity, manipulative bundle architecture); **algorithmic fairness audit** for any randomized reward system; **age-gating and spend-protection** (hard caps for minors, crisis-intervention alerts, parental controls). | **EU**: Chance-based reward for real money **banned/replaced**; deterministic direct-purchase, battle-pass, or cosmetic-only progression only. **Korea/China**: Chance permitted with **legally prescribed disclosure format** and government filing/approval. **Japan**: Gacha permitted; **gift-system and cosmetic prestige** are primary revenue drivers; **kompu gacha banned**; disclosure present but culturally framed. **Gulf**: Chance mechanics **restricted/reframed**; emphasis on **direct luxury purchase, exclusivity, and status gifting**; explicit gambling framing avoided. **Brazil**: P2W mechanics must be **clearly separated** from competitive/progression systems; direct-purchase alternatives emphasized; advocacy-observed fairness required. **US**: Mechanic permitted where legal, but **state-level disclosure and deterministic alternatives** required in high-risk states; litigation-defensible documentation mandatory. | Do not apply Korea/China government XML filing templates to Japan gift-culture events (they serve different credibility mechanisms); do not apply EU deterministic-ban logic to Gulf luxury-status mechanics (they destroy legitimate revenue and cultural fit); do not apply Brazil advocacy-bargaining norms to US litigation defense (they miss evidentiary requirements); do not allow US cross-border advocacy campaigns to dictate EU regulatory compliance timelines. |
| **Probability Disclosure & Transparency** | Where any randomization exists, **truthful, complete, localized-language disclosure** of probabilities and item pools; no hidden or aggregated misleading statistics; player-accessible audit portal. | **EU**: Not applicable for banned mechanics; for deterministic alternatives, **full pricing and content transparency** in local advertising-law format; GDPR-linked behavioral-data access rights. **Korea/China**: **Legally prescribed format** (probability tables, item lists, approval stamps); government-filed and in-app rendered identically; bilingual master required. **Japan**: Disclosure present as **trust-building visual table** (not only legal warning); integrated into gift-event and cosmetic-prestige framing; community-friendly design. **Gulf**: Transparency framed as **ethical commitment/exclusivity verification**; avoids “gambling-risk” language; government content-review documentation prioritized. **Brazil**: Disclosure in **Portuguese + English master**; advocacy-group observation access; P2W separation clearly documented; price-context transparency included. **US**: **State-compliant layered disclosure**; English-language master archive with state annotations; litigation-hold documentation protocol active. | Do not provide EU-level individual behavioral data dumps to Brazilian informal advocacy leaders (violates privacy and undermines legitimacy); do not limit Korea/China government filings to “marketing-style” visual summaries—legal evidentiary standards apply; do not suppress Japanese community-requested transparency through “global minimal disclosure.” |
| **Event Calendar & Cultural Framing** | **Anti-deceptive event design**: no false urgency, no hidden cost escalation, no culturally inappropriate content; crisis-escalation pathway open globally. | **EU**: Event calendar tied to **regulatory audit and national advertising-enforcement windows**; no seasonal chance-events. **Korea/China**: Calendar tied to **approval-filing deadlines**; event updates filed before activation. **Japan**: Calendar tied to **gift-giving and prestige seasons** (New Year, Golden Week, seasonal reciprocity); events designed for **social harmony and collective participation**. **Gulf**: Calendar tied to **religious months** (Ramadan, Eid) and government review windows; luxury/exclusivity framing verified with cultural advisors. **Brazil**: Calendar tied to **advocacy-watch periods** and government self-regulatory reporting; direct-purchase fairness updates prioritized. **US**: Calendar tied to **legislative session and advocacy-campaign windows**; cross-state consistency maintained where possible. | Do not export Japan gift-event mechanics to EU markets without removing chance/replacing with deterministic rewards; do not apply Gulf luxury-status framing in Brazil without price-access adaptation; do not use US litigation-defense language in Gulf private mediation. |
| **Player Representation & Advocacy Engagement** | Anti-retaliation for collective/player advocacy participation; transparency portal accessible; crisis-escalation pathway open; no suppression of legitimate advocacy through “independent player” rhetoric. | **EU**: Official regulatory/advocacy complaint pathways; formal documentation. **Korea/China**: Government certification and formal observation rights dominate; advocacy engaged through regulatory compliance verification. **Japan**: Peer-verified community leader bridge + government Consumer Affairs; face-saving private revision first; digital sentiment command. **Gulf**: Government mediator + luxury-community advisory; private face-saving revision; status/community influencer verification. **Brazil**: Peer-verified informal collective leader + formal advocacy-group liaison; direct negotiation boundary clear; government mediator in formal rounds. **US**: Certified advocacy-group and litigation partner; formal observation and discovery-ready documentation; cross-border advocacy coordination tracked. | Do not deny Brazil advocacy groups formal documentation rights to “protect informality”; do not force EU-style formal election requirements onto Japan peer-verified community leaders; do not apply Japan private-revision norms to US litigation processes where formal documentation protects both sides. |

### 4. Staggered Rollout: The “Staggered Evidence” Monetization Model

Launching all six profiles simultaneously with a single global loot-box table and event calendar is operationally efficient but structurally catastrophic. The rollout treats **EU formal restriction** as the **regulatory-authority foundation** (highest documentation rigor, generates master replacement-mechanic protocol), **East Asia** as the **disclosure-formal and cultural-scale anchor** (largest mature markets with government and social dynamics), and the **remaining markets** as **defense and synthesis extensions**.

| Phase | Timeline | Cluster / Region | Integration Mode | Strategic Objective | Key Actions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Formal Restriction Foundation** | Months 1–4 | **EU (Belgium / Netherlands)** | **Formal Restriction & Replacement Integration**. Highest regulatory formality; strictest mechanic-ban documentation; generates master **“No-Chance-Reward / Deterministic Alternative” protocol** and disclosure architecture. | Stabilize L1 ethical backbone; generate **Reference Monetization Playbook** (deterministic direct-purchase framework, GDPR-aligned behavioral transparency, anti-dark-pattern audit, regulatory-filing template); protect market access from ban/enforcement. | • Joint “Mechanic Replacement & Transparency Workshop”: global monetization policy rendered into EU-context documentation with regulatory authority verification; deterministic progression paths engineered and certified.<br>• Pilot rollout: limited-market release of replacement mechanics (battle-pass, direct cosmetic store) with official authority observation; private clarification pathway established before public launch.<br>• Lock disclosure-documentation format and anti-pattern audit framework into global Monetization Integration Registry.<br>• Build regulatory-calendar annex (filing, audit, advertising-enforcement windows) linked to live-ops planning. |
| **Phase 2: Disclosure Formal & Cultural Scale** | Months 3–8 | **Korea & China** + **Japan** (parallel, separate L2 tracks) | **Government Certification & Disclosure Protocol (Korea/China)**; **Cultural Consensus & Gift-Event Protocol (Japan)**. Adapt EU formal rigor to government filing and to high-context cultural scale—without copying either logic. | Secure government-certified market access in East Asia; honor Japan’s mature gacha/gift culture with face-saving governance; prevent cross-contamination (government filing does not become gift-culture framing; gift-culture informality does not weaken filing discipline). | • Hire **Local Monetization Integrity Directors** in Seoul/Shanghai/Tokyo—not remote HQ live-ops managers.<br>• **Korea/China**: Launch government-file certification round; probability disclosure rendered in legally prescribed format; approval-cycle timeline integrated into event calendar; bilingual (local + English master) filing archive built; advocacy observation rights formalized with certified partners.<br>• **Japan**: Launch “Community Consensus Workshops”: peer-verified community leaders (streamers, guild heads) observe feature changes; gift-event calendar co-designed; private face-saving revision pathway tested; digital-monitoring command activated for sentiment velocity; transparency portal localized with visual/social design.<br>• Lock separate playbooks; prevent cross-export of disclosure templates. |
| **Phase 3: Emerging Defense & Cross-Region Synthesis** |
